explain.say: What if I told you that people in the rainforests of Mexico and Central America used a sign for zero over 1,500 years ago? They were the Maya, and their people still live there today. The timeline shows their long story.

explain.say: See the calendar? Maya writers carved dates in stone, using a dot for one, a bar for five, and a shell for zero. They tracked the Sun, Moon and Venus very carefully. Can you make seven with bars and dots? One bar and two dots!

faq.a: Cities like Tikal, Palenque and Copan had tall stone pyramid temples, palaces, plazas and ball courts, surrounded by farms. Each had its own king, and cities often allied or fought.

faq.q: How did the Maya write numbers?
faq.a: They used a dot for one, a bar for five and a shell shape for zero, in a system based on twenties. For example, seven is one bar and two dots.
asks: Did the Maya have a zero?

faq.a: Many southern cities emptied in the 800s and 900s. Evidence points to long droughts, too many people for the land, and wars between cities, all working together.

faq.q: What happened when the Spanish arrived?
faq.a: From the 1520s Spanish forces fought Maya kingdoms for more than 150 years. The last independent Maya city, Nojpeten, fell in 1697. Many books were burned and many people died from new diseases.
Yes. Several million Maya people live in Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, Honduras and El Salvador today, and around 30 Mayan languages are still spoken.

facts: Only four Maya books, called codices, are known to survive.
The Maya used a shell-shaped sign for zero in a number system based on twenty.
Nojpeten, the last independent Maya kingdom, fell to Spain in 1697.

quiz.say: How would the Maya write the number seven?
quiz.why: A bar is five and each dot is one, so five plus two makes seven.

wrong.2: Two bars make ten, not seven.

quiz.show: What happened to the Maya people?
quiz.why: Millions of Maya people live in Mexico and Central America today.

wrong.1: Some cities emptied around 900, but the people moved and lived on.
wrong.2: Maya people stayed in their homelands.
